sanskrit: manda̍sva ho̱trād anu̱ joṣa̱m andha̱so 'dhva̍ryava̱ḥ sa pū̱rṇāṁ va̍ṣṭy ā̱sica̍m | tasmā̍ e̱tam bha̍rata tadva̱śo da̱dir ho̱trāt soma̍ṁ draviṇoda̱ḥ piba̍ ṛ̱tubhi̍ḥ ||
english: Be gladdened, O Adhvaryus, according to your pleasure from the Hotṛ's share of the soma-juice — he who desires a full vessel of the libation. Bring therefore this draught to him, the generous giver, obedient to his will: drink the soma from the Hotṛ's cup, O Draviṇodas, at the (proper) seasons.

sanskrit: yam u̱ pūrva̱m ahu̍ve̱ tam i̱daṁ hu̍ve̱ sed u̱ havyo̍ da̱dir yo nāma̱ patya̍te | a̱dhva̱ryubhi̱ḥ prasthi̍taṁ so̱myam madhu̍ po̱trāt soma̍ṁ draviṇoda̱ḥ piba̍ ṛ̱tubhi̍ḥ ||
english: Him whom I invoked aforetime, that same one I invoke now — he is indeed worthy of invocation, the liberal giver who rules by his very name. Drink the sweet soma-draught set forth by the Adhvaryus from the Potṛ's cup, O Draviṇodas, at the (proper) seasons.

sanskrit: medya̍ntu te̱ vahna̍yo̱ yebhi̱r īya̱se 'ri̍ṣaṇyan vīḻayasvā vanaspate | ā̱yūyā̍ dhṛṣṇo abhi̱gūryā̱ tvaṁ ne̱ṣṭrāt soma̍ṁ draviṇoda̱ḥ piba̍ ṛ̱tubhi̍ḥ ||
english: Let your carriers be purified — those by which you travel, unharmed; be you firm, O Vanaspati. Bold one, having roared forth with your fierce cry, drink the soma from the Neṣṭṛ's cup, O Draviṇodas, at the (proper) seasons.

sanskrit: apā̍d dho̱trād u̱ta po̱trād a̍matto̱ta ne̱ṣṭrād a̍juṣata̱ prayo̍ hi̱tam | tu̱rīya̱m pātra̱m amṛ̍kta̱m ama̍rtyaṁ draviṇo̱dāḥ pi̍batu drāviṇoda̱saḥ ||
english: Not from the Hotṛ's cup, nor from the Potṛ's has he drunk to satiety, nor did he relish the oblation set forth from the Neṣṭṛ's cup. Let Draviṇodas drink from the fourth vessel, uncontaminated and immortal, belonging to the Son of Draviṇodas.

sanskrit: a̱rvāñca̍m a̱dya ya̱yya̍ṁ nṛ̱vāha̍ṇa̱ṁ ratha̍ṁ yuñjāthām i̱ha vā̍ṁ vi̱moca̍nam | pṛ̱ṅktaṁ ha̱vīṁṣi̱ madhu̱nā hi ka̍ṁ ga̱tam athā̱ soma̍m pibataṁ vājinīvasū ||
english: Harness your swift chariot, man-borne and fit for travel, hither today — here shall be your unyoking. The oblations are mingled with honey; come then, and drink the soma, O ye two whose wealth is in strength (Vājinīvasū — the Aśvins).

sanskrit: joṣy a̍gne sa̱midha̱ṁ joṣy āhu̍ti̱ṁ joṣi̱ brahma̱ janya̱ṁ joṣi̍ suṣṭu̱tim | viśve̍bhi̱r viśvā̍m̐ ṛ̱tunā̍ vaso ma̱ha u̱śan de̱vām̐ u̍śa̱taḥ pā̍yayā ha̱viḥ ||
english: Be pleased, O Agni, with the kindling-wood; be pleased with the oblation; be pleased with the brahman (prayer) belonging to the people; be pleased with the hymn of praise. O Vasu, great one, with all the gods at the (proper) season, being yourself desirous, make the desirous gods drink the oblation.

sanskrit: ud u̱ ṣya de̱vaḥ sa̍vi̱tā sa̱vāya̍ śaśvatta̱maṁ tada̍pā̱ vahni̍r asthāt | nū̱naṁ de̱vebhyo̱ vi hi dhāti̱ ratna̱m athābha̍jad vī̱tiho̍traṁ sva̱stau ||
english: Up has risen this god Savitṛ for his stimulation; the ever-constant carrier (of offerings) has taken his stand thereby. Now he distributes treasure among the gods, and has shared out (his gifts) with the fire of offering in blessing.

sanskrit: viśva̍sya̱ hi śru̱ṣṭaye̍ de̱va ū̱rdhvaḥ pra bā̱havā̍ pṛ̱thupā̍ṇi̱ḥ sisa̍rti | āpa̍ś cid asya vra̱ta ā nimṛ̍grā a̱yaṁ ci̱d vāto̍ ramate̱ pari̍jman ||
english: For the hearing of all, the god rises upright, extending his two arms with broad hands. Even the waters sink down at his ordinance; even this wind rests in its circuit.

sanskrit: ā̱śubhi̍ś ci̱d yān vi mu̍cāti nū̱nam arī̍rama̱d ata̍mānaṁ ci̱d eto̍ḥ | a̱hyarṣū̍ṇāṁ ci̱n ny a̍yām̐ avi̱ṣyām anu̍ vra̱taṁ sa̍vi̱tur moky āgā̍t ||
english: Even those (steeds) which he now unyokes with the swiftest, even the untamed course has rested. Even the paths of the water-rushing serpents have been laid down; following the ordinance of Savitṛ, (the world) has come to release.

sanskrit: puna̱ḥ sam a̍vya̱d vita̍ta̱ṁ vaya̍ntī ma̱dhyā karto̱r ny a̍dhā̱c chakma̱ dhīra̍ḥ | ut sa̱ṁhāyā̍sthā̱d vy ṛ1̱̍tūm̐r a̍dardhar a̱rama̍tiḥ savi̱tā de̱va āgā̍t ||
english: She who weaves has again rolled up what was spread out; the wise one has laid down her skill in the midst of her work. The divine Savitṛ, Aramatī (Piety), has risen up, having shaken apart the seasons.

sanskrit: nānaukā̍ṁsi̱ duryo̱ viśva̱m āyu̱r vi ti̍ṣṭhate prabha̱vaḥ śoko̍ a̱gneḥ | jyeṣṭha̍m mā̱tā sū̱nave̍ bhā̱gam ādhā̱d anv a̍sya̱ keta̍m iṣi̱taṁ sa̍vi̱trā ||
english: The abodes of diverse forms pervade all of life throughout the house — such is the power, the flame of Agni. The mother has assigned the best portion to her son; Savitṛ has impelled (men to act) following his will.

sanskrit: sa̱māva̍varti̱ viṣṭhi̍to jigī̱ṣur viśve̍ṣā̱ṁ kāma̱ś cara̍tām a̱mābhū̍t | śaśvā̱m̐ apo̱ vikṛ̍taṁ hi̱tvy āgā̱d anu̍ vra̱taṁ sa̍vi̱tur daivya̍sya ||
english: Having taken his stance, eager to conquer, he (the sun) has wheeled back; the desire of all who roam about has come home. Leaving behind the ever-flowing waters in their altered state, he has come back following the divine ordinance of Savitṛ.

sanskrit: tvayā̍ hi̱tam apya̍m a̱psu bhā̱gaṁ dhanvānv ā mṛ̍ga̱yaso̱ vi ta̍sthuḥ | vanā̍ni̱ vibhyo̱ naki̍r asya̱ tāni̍ vra̱tā de̱vasya̍ savi̱tur mi̍nanti ||
english: The share of water-dwelling (creatures) placed by you in the waters — the gazelles tracking across the desert have spread out (to their own places). No one violates the woodlands (which belong) to the various (creatures); none transgress the ordinances of the divine Savitṛ.

sanskrit: yā̱drā̱dhya1̱̍ṁ varu̍ṇo̱ yoni̱m apya̍m a̱ni̍śitaṁ ni̱miṣi̱ jarbhu̍rāṇaḥ | viśvo̍ mārtā̱ṇḍo vra̱jam ā pa̱śur gā̍t stha̱śo janmā̍ni savi̱tā vy āka̍ḥ ||
english: Where Varuṇa lies unsleeping, blinking in the watery womb — every living creature, Mārtāṇḍa (the sun-bird), has gone to the fold; Savitṛ has declared the births of those that stand (on the earth).

sanskrit: na yasyendro̱ varu̍ṇo̱ na mi̱tro vra̱tam a̍rya̱mā na mi̍nanti̍ ru̱draḥ | nārā̍taya̱s tam i̱daṁ sva̱sti hu̱ve de̱vaṁ sa̍vi̱tāra̱ṁ namo̍bhiḥ ||
english: Whose ordinance neither Indra, nor Varuṇa, nor Mitra, nor Aryaman, nor Rudra violates, nor do hostile powers — him, this divine Savitṛ, I now invoke for blessing with reverences.

sanskrit: bhaga̱ṁ dhiya̍ṁ vā̱jaya̍nta̱ḥ pura̍ṁdhi̱ṁ narā̱śaṁso̱ gnāspati̍r no avyāḥ ||  ā̱ye vā̱masya̍ saṁga̱the ra̍yī̱ṇām pri̱yā de̱vasya̍ savi̱tuḥ syā̍ma ||
english: Striving for Bhaga, for wise understanding, for eloquence — may Narāśaṁsa and Gnāspati protect us. May we be dear to the divine Savitṛ at the confluence of riches, at the gathering-place of wealth.

sanskrit: a̱smabhya̱ṁ tad di̱vo a̱dbhyaḥ pṛ̍thi̱vyās tvayā̍ da̱ttaṁ kāmya̱ṁ rādha̱ ā gā̍t | śaṁ yat sto̱tṛbhya ā̱paye̱ bhavā̍ty uru̱śaṁsā̍ya savitar jari̱tre ||
english: May the desirable bounty from heaven, from the waters, from the earth, given by you, come to us. That which brings blessing to the praisers, to the one who seeks refreshment — O Savitṛ, widely acclaimed, to your singer.

sanskrit: grāvā̍ṇeva̱ tad id artha̍ṁ jarethe̱ gṛdhre̍va vṛ̱kṣaṁ ni̍dhi̱manta̱m accha̍ | bra̱hmāṇe̍va vi̱datha̍ uktha̱śāsā̍ dū̱teva̱ havyā̱ janyā̍ puru̱trā ||
english: Like two pressing-stones you praise that very purpose; like a vulture toward a tree that holds a treasure. Like two chanters of brahman in the assembly, reciting the uktha-verse; like two messengers (you convey) the oblations belonging to the people in many places.

sanskrit: prā̱ta̱ryāvā̍ṇā ra̱thye̍va vī̱rājeva̍ ya̱mā vara̱m ā sa̍cethe | mene̍ iva ta̱nvā̱3̱̍ śumbha̍māne̱ dampa̍tīva kratu̱vidā̱ jane̍ṣu ||
english: Going forth at dawn, like two chariot-warriors, like two Yamas you attain the boon together. Like two women adorning their bodies, like a husband and wife knowing (the proper) rites among the people.

sanskrit: śṛṅge̍va naḥ pratha̱mā ga̍ntam a̱rvāk cha̱phāv i̍va̱ jarbhu̍rāṇā̱ taro̍bhiḥ | ca̱kra̱vā̱keva̱ prati̱ vasto̍r usrā̱rvāñcā̍ yātaṁ ra̱thye̍va śakrā ||
english: Come first to us as the (two) horns (of an animal), gnawing powerfully like two hooves. Come hither at dawn like two ruddy geese (cakravākas) at the break of day, like two capable chariot-warriors.

sanskrit: nā̱veva̍ naḥ pārayataṁ yu̱geva̱ nabhye̍va na upa̱dhīva̍ pra̱dhīva̍ | śvāne̍va no̱ ari̍ṣaṇyā ta̱nūnā̱ṁ khṛga̍leva vi̱srasa̍ḥ pātam a̱smān ||
english: Like a boat, carry us across; like a yoke, (uphold us) like the nave (of a wheel), like the felloe, like the circumference. Like a dog, keep our bodies from injury; like the khṛgala-bird (which warns), protect us from calamity.

sanskrit: vāte̍vāju̱ryā na̱dye̍va rī̱tir a̱kṣī i̍va̱ cakṣu̱ṣā yā̍tam a̱rvāk | hastā̍v iva ta̱nve̱3̱̍ śambha̍viṣṭhā̱ pāde̍va no nayata̱ṁ vasyo̱ accha̍ ||
english: Come hither like the aging (rush) of wind, like the flowing of a river, like two eyes with their sight. Most beneficent for our body, like two hands — like two feet, lead us toward (greater) well-being.

sanskrit: oṣṭhā̍v iva̱ madhv ā̱sne vada̍ntā̱ stanā̍v iva pipyataṁ jī̱vase̍ naḥ | nāse̍va nas ta̱nvo̍ rakṣi̱tārā̱ karṇā̍v iva su̱śrutā̍ bhūtam a̱sme ||
english: Like two lips speaking sweetness into the mouth, like two breasts, fill us (with nourishment) for life. Like two nostrils, be the guardians of our body; like two ears, be you sharp-hearing among us.

sanskrit: haste̍va śa̱ktim a̱bhi sa̍ṁda̱dī na̱ḥ kṣāme̍va na̱ḥ sam a̍jata̱ṁ rajā̍ṁsi | i̱mā giro̍ aśvinā yuṣma̱yantī̱ḥ kṣṇotre̍ṇeva̱ svadhi̍ti̱ṁ saṁ śi̍śītam ||
english: Like a hand, bestow power on us; like the earth, gather together our (scattered) spaces. These songs, O Aśvins, yearning for you — sharpen them like an axe on a whetstone.

sanskrit: e̱tāni̍ vām aśvinā̱ vardha̍nāni̱ brahma̱ stoma̍ṁ gṛtsama̱dāso̍ akran | tāni̍ narā jujuṣā̱ṇopa̍ yātam bṛ̱had va̍dema vi̱dathe̍ su̱vīrā̍ḥ ||
english: These (words) that strengthen you, O Aśvins — the Gṛtsamadas have made (this) brahman-hymn of praise. O ye two heroes, come delighting in them; may we speak the great (word) in the assembly, endowed with good heroes.

sanskrit: somā̍pūṣaṇā̱ jana̍nā rayī̱ṇāṁ jana̍nā di̱vo jana̍nā pṛthi̱vyāḥ | jā̱tau viśva̍sya̱ bhuva̍nasya go̱pau de̱vā a̍kṛṇvann a̱mṛta̍sya̱ nābhi̍m ||
english: O Soma and Pūṣan, generators of riches, generators of heaven, generators of earth — the two guardians born of all existence — the gods made you the navel of immortality.

sanskrit: i̱mau de̱vau jāya̍mānau juṣante̱mau tamā̍ṁsi gūhatā̱m aju̍ṣṭā | ā̱bhyām indra̍ḥ pa̱kvam ā̱māsv a̱ntaḥ so̍māpū̱ṣabhyā̍ṁ janad u̱sriyā̍su ||
english: These two gods as they are being born show favor; let these two conceal the undesired darknesses. Through these two — Soma and Pūṣan — Indra generated the ripe (cattle) within the raw (stones), among the ruddy cows (of dawn).

sanskrit: somā̍pūṣaṇā̱ raja̍so vi̱māna̱ṁ sa̱ptaca̍kra̱ṁ ratha̱m avi̍śvaminvam | vi̱ṣū̱vṛta̱m mana̍sā yu̱jyamā̍na̱ṁ taṁ ji̍nvatho vṛṣaṇā̱ pañca̍raśmim ||
english: O Soma and Pūṣan, the measure of the atmosphere is the seven-wheeled chariot that pervades all space — turning in opposite directions, yoked by the mind: that chariot with five reins, O ye two bulls, you impel.

sanskrit: di̱vy a1̱̍nyaḥ sada̍naṁ ca̱kra u̱ccā pṛ̍thi̱vyām a̱nyo adhy a̱ntari̍kṣe | tāv a̱smabhya̍m puru̱vāra̍m puru̱kṣuṁ rā̱yas poṣa̱ṁ vi ṣya̍tā̱ṁ nābhi̍m a̱sme ||
english: One has made his seat on high in heaven; the other (moves) above the earth in mid-air. Let those two release for us the navel of abundant bounty, the richly-nourishing pouring-forth of riches, upon us.

sanskrit: viśvā̍ny a̱nyo bhuva̍nā ja̱jāna̱ viśva̍m a̱nyo a̍bhi̱cakṣā̍ṇa eti | somā̍pūṣaṇā̱v ava̍ta̱ṁ dhiya̍m me yu̱vābhyā̱ṁ viśvā̱ḥ pṛta̍nā jayema ||
english: One has engendered all the worlds; the other moves beholding everything. O Soma and Pūṣan, strengthen my thought; through you both may we conquer all opposing hosts.

sanskrit: dhiya̍m pū̱ṣā ji̍nvatu viśvami̱nvo ra̱yiṁ somo̍ rayi̱pati̍r dadhātu | ava̍tu de̱vy adi̍tir ana̱rvā bṛ̱had va̍dema vi̱dathe̍ su̱vīrā̍ḥ ||
english: May Pūṣan, all-pervading, quicken (our) thought; may Soma, lord of riches, establish wealth. May the divine, unassailable Aditi protect (us); may we speak the great (word) in the assembly, endowed with good heroes.

sanskrit: vāyo̱ ye te̍ saha̱sriṇo̱ rathā̍sa̱s tebhi̱r ā ga̍hi | ni̱yutvā̱n soma̍pītaye ||
english: O Vāyu, come hither with those thousandfold chariots of yours, drawn by your team, to drink the soma.

sanskrit: ni̱yutvā̍n vāya̱v ā ga̍hy a̱yaṁ śu̱kro a̍yāmi te | gantā̍si sunva̱to gṛ̱ham ||
english: O Vāyu, with your team come hither — this bright (soma) is poured out for you. You shall be one who goes to the house of the soma-presser.

sanskrit: śu̱krasyā̱dya gavā̍śira̱ indra̍vāyū ni̱yutva̍taḥ | ā yā̍ta̱m piba̍taṁ narā ||
english: Of the bright (soma) mixed today with milk — O Indra and Vāyu, with your teams, come hither, O ye two heroes, and drink.

sanskrit: a̱yaṁ vā̍m mitrāvaruṇā su̱taḥ soma̍ ṛtāvṛdhā | mamed i̱ha śru̍ta̱ṁ hava̍m ||
english: O Mitra and Varuṇa, increasers of truth (ṛta) — this soma is pressed out for you both. Hear my invocation here.

sanskrit: rājā̍nā̱v ana̍bhidruhā dhru̱ve sada̍sy u̱ttame̱ | sa̱hasra̍sthūṇa āsāte ||
english: The two kings without treachery are seated in the firm, highest assembly — the hall with a thousand pillars.

sanskrit: tā sa̱mrājā̍ ghṛ̱tāsu̍tī ādi̱tyā dānu̍na̱s patī̍ | sace̍te̱ ana̍vahvaram ||
english: Those two universal sovereigns, for whom ghee is poured, the two Ādityas, lords of the gift (dānu) — they associate without deviation.

sanskrit: goma̍d ū̱ ṣu nā̍sa̱tyāśvā̍vad yātam aśvinā | va̱rtī ru̍drā nṛ̱pāyya̍m ||
english: O Nāsatyas, O Aśvins — come hither with (gifts of) cattle, with horses. O Rudra (sons of Rudra), bring the wealth worthy of heroes.

sanskrit: na yat paro̱ nānta̍ra āda̱dharṣa̍d vṛṣaṇvasū | du̱ḥśaṁso̱ martyo̍ ri̱puḥ ||
english: That no malicious mortal enemy from without or from within might do harm to you, O ye two whose wealth is the bull (Vṛṣaṇvasū — the Aśvins).

sanskrit: tā na̱ ā vo̍ḻham aśvinā ra̱yim pi̱śaṅga̍saṁdṛśam | dhiṣṇyā̍ varivo̱vida̍m ||
english: O Aśvins, bring us here the wealth of tawny aspect, O ye attentive ones, that finds wide space.

sanskrit: indro̍ a̱ṅga ma̱had bha̱yam a̱bhī ṣad apa̍ cucyavat | sa hi sthi̱ro vica̍rṣaṇiḥ ||
english: Indra, truly, has shaken off great terror from here; for he is the firm one, the all-seeing.

sanskrit: indra̍ś ca mṛ̱ḻayā̍ti no̱ na na̍ḥ pa̱ścād a̱ghaṁ na̍śat | bha̱dram bha̍vāti naḥ pu̱raḥ ||
english: And may Indra be gracious to us; let no evil overtake us from behind; may blessedness be before us.

sanskrit: indra̱ āśā̍bhya̱s pari̱ sarvā̍bhyo̱ abha̍yaṁ karat | jetā̱ śatrū̱n vica̍rṣaṇiḥ ||
english: May Indra make (us) fearless on every side, on all quarters — the all-seeing conqueror of enemies.

sanskrit: viśve̍ devāsa̱ ā ga̍ta śṛṇu̱tā ma̍ i̱maṁ hava̍m | edam ba̱rhir ni ṣī̍data ||
english: O all-gods (Viśvedevāḥ), come hither; hear this invocation of mine; sit down upon this barhis-grass.

sanskrit: tī̱vro vo̱ madhu̍mām̐ a̱yaṁ śu̱naho̍treṣu matsa̱raḥ | e̱tam pi̍bata̱ kāmya̍m ||
english: This intoxicating (soma), pungent and sweet, for you in the rites of the Śunahotras — drink this desirable (draught).

sanskrit: indra̍jyeṣṭhā̱ maru̍dgaṇā̱ devā̍sa̱ḥ pūṣa̍rātayaḥ | viśve̱ mama̍ śrutā̱ hava̍m ||
english: The Marut-hosts with Indra as their chief, the gods with Pūṣan as their gift-giver — all of you, hear my invocation.

sanskrit: ambi̍tame̱ nadī̍tame̱ devi̍tame̱ sara̍svati | a̱pra̱śa̱stā i̍va smasi̱ praśa̍stim amba nas kṛdhi ||
english: O Sarasvatī, best of mothers, best of rivers, best of goddesses — we are as though without praise; O mother, make praise for us.

sanskrit: tve viśvā̍ sarasvati śri̱tāyū̍ṁṣi de̱vyām | śu̱naho̍treṣu matsva pra̱jāṁ de̍vi didiḍḍhi naḥ ||
english: In you, O Sarasvatī divine, all life-forces are sheltered. Find joy in the rites of the Śunahotras; O goddess, shine upon our progeny.

sanskrit: i̱mā brahma̍ sarasvati ju̱ṣasva̍ vājinīvati | yā te̱ manma̍ gṛtsama̱dā ṛ̍tāvari pri̱yā de̱veṣu̱ juhva̍ti ||
english: Be pleased, O Sarasvatī possessed of sustenance (Vājinīvatī), with this brahman-prayer — the devotion that the Gṛtsamadas, O guardian of truth (ṛtāvari), dear to the gods, offer up to you.

sanskrit: pretā̍ṁ ya̱jñasya̍ śa̱mbhuvā̍ yu̱vām id ā vṛ̍ṇīmahe | a̱gniṁ ca̍ havya̱vāha̍nam ||
english: We choose only you two, the two beneficent ones presiding over the sacrifice, to go forth — and Agni the bearer of oblations.

sanskrit: dyāvā̍ naḥ pṛthi̱vī i̱maṁ si̱dhram a̱dya di̍vi̱spṛśa̍m | ya̱jñaṁ de̱veṣu̍ yacchatām ||
english: May Heaven and Earth today direct this successful, sky-touching sacrifice among the gods.

sanskrit: ā vā̍m u̱pastha̍m adruhā de̱vāḥ sī̍dantu ya̱jñiyā̍ḥ | i̱hādya soma̍pītaye ||
english: In your lap, O ye two without treachery, let the divine and holy powers sit here today for the drinking of soma.

sanskrit: kani̍kradaj ja̱nuṣa̍m prabruvā̱ṇa iya̍rti̱ vāca̍m ari̱teva̱ nāva̍m | su̱ma̱ṅgala̍ś ca śakune̱ bhavā̍si̱ mā tvā̱ kā ci̍d abhi̱bhā viśvyā̍ vidat ||
english: Crying again and again, announcing (yourself) by your birth-cry, you set your voice in motion like a rower his boat. Be you of auspicious omen, O bird; may no universal misfortune find you.

sanskrit: mā tvā̍ śye̱na ud va̍dhī̱n mā su̍pa̱rṇo mā tvā̍ vida̱d iṣu̍mān vī̱ro astā̍ | pitryā̱m anu̍ pra̱diśa̱ṁ kani̍kradat suma̱ṅgalo̍ bhadravā̱dī va̍de̱ha ||
english: Let not the hawk slay you, nor the eagle; let not the armed warrior-archer find you. Crying again and again in the direction of the ancestors, speak here as an auspicious, good-word-speaking one.

sanskrit: ava̍ kranda dakṣiṇa̱to gṛ̱hāṇā̍ṁ suma̱ṅgalo̍ bhadravā̱dī śa̍kunte | mā na̍ḥ ste̱na ī̍śata̱ māghaśa̍ṁso bṛ̱had va̍dema vi̱dathe̍ su̱vīrā̍ḥ ||
english: Cry down (your omen) from the south upon our houses, auspicious and good-word-speaking, O bird (śakunta). Let no thief gain power over us, no wicked one; may we speak the great (word) in the assembly, endowed with good heroes.

sanskrit: pra̱da̱kṣi̱ṇid a̱bhi gṛ̍ṇanti kā̱ravo̱ vayo̱ vada̍nta ṛtu̱thā śa̱kunta̍yaḥ | u̱bhe vācau̍ vadati sāma̱gā i̍va gāya̱traṁ ca̱ traiṣṭu̍bha̱ṁ cānu̍ rājati ||
english: The śakunta-birds (kārus) sing circling sunwise; the birds speak in their proper season. It (the bird) utters both voices as though a sāman-singer — it reigns over the gāyatrī and the triṣṭubh in succession.

sanskrit: u̱dgā̱teva̍ śakune̱ sāma̍ gāyasi brahmapu̱tra i̍va̱ sava̍neṣu śaṁsasi | vṛṣe̍va vā̱jī śiśu̍matīr a̱pītyā̍ sa̱rvato̍ naḥ śakune bha̱dram ā va̍da vi̱śvato̍ naḥ śakune̱ puṇya̱m ā va̍da ||
english: Like an Udgātṛ, O bird, you sing the sāman; like a brahman's son you recite at the soma-pressings. Like a powerful bull (going) to the nursing cows, proclaim blessings to us from every side, O bird; proclaim what is auspicious to us from all directions, O bird.

sanskrit: ā̱vada̱m̐s tvaṁ śa̍kune bha̱dram ā va̍da tū̱ṣṇīm āsī̍naḥ suma̱tiṁ ci̍kiddhi naḥ | yad u̱tpata̱n vada̍si karka̱rir ya̍thā bṛ̱had va̍dema vi̱dathe̍ su̱vīrā̍ḥ ||
english: You who are speaking, O bird, speak blessings; even sitting in silence, discern well-being for us. When you speak as you fly up, like the karkarī (calling bird) — may we speak the great (word) in the assembly, endowed with good heroes.
